newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-EL GUERROUJ SETS WORLD RECORD IN 1500 METRES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EL GUERROUJ SETS WORLD RECORD IN 1500 METRES.

text.p: Morocco's Hicham El Guerrouj shattered a six-year-old world indoor record in the 1500 metres by three seconds at an international athletics meeting in Stuttgart on Sunday.
Britain's Linford Christie also enjoyed a good day as he came from behind to win the 200 metres although he was narrowly denied a double in the 60 metre sprint by Jamaican Michael Green.
El Guerrouj, the 1995 indoor champion, won the 1500 metre race in a time of three minutes 31.18 seconds, smashing the previous record of 3:34.16 set by Noureddine Morceli of Algeria in Spain in 1991.
Ethiopia's Haile Gebreselassie came in second in a time of 3:32.39 at the 1.1 million mark ($700,000) event which attracted 7,500 spectators.

"My training went very well before this race and I am thrilled. Everything went well," said El Guerrouj, who fell in the Atlanta Olympics. "I had a very hard time at the Olympics. It was a difficult time."
Christie, the 1992 Olympic champion over 100 metres, came from behind to clock the same time of 6.56 seconds as Green in the 60 metre race but was pipped for first place in the photo finish.
Less than an hour later Christie was back on the 200 metre oval track and powerfully bolted from behind to win the 200 metres in a time of 20.70 seconds.

In the women's 60 metre event, Christa Opara of Nigeria equalled the world's fastest time this year with a time of 7.08 seconds while Olympic 100 metre champion Gail Devers came in a disappointing fifth with a time of 7.10 seconds.
Britain's Colin Jackson won the 60 metre hurdles in a time of 7.47 seconds.
Michelle Freeman of Jamaica won the women's event in 7.91 seconds, another world best for 1997 while Germany's Grit Breuer won the 400 metres in 51.50 seconds.
Germany's Heike Drechsler took the long jump with a leap of 6.95 metres and said she soon expected to hit the seven metre mark again.
"I am quite surprised I jumped so well today," she said. "I have more self-confidence and believe I will soon be over seven metres again."
Nico Motchebon of Germany won the 800 metre race in a time of 1:46.40 seconds.
